"Closing the door to sleep is for those of the highest capacity."
Looking into the mirror and stretching repeatedly—this is merely for those of middling or inferior capacity.

Case: Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty asked Master Bodhidharma, "Since you have risen this morning, have you not yet made a profit? What is the primary meaning of the Noble Truths? He then asked about the secondary level. Bodhidharma said: [The Emperor] asked: "What is the primary meaning of the Noble Truths? Bodhidharma replied: "I do not speak of it. The Emperor asked again: "Why do you not speak of it? Bodhidharma said: "Because you do not believe me. The Emperor asked: "How can I come to believe you? Bodhidharma said: "If you wish to believe me, you must first cast off your imperial body; once you have cast it off, you will naturally come to believe me. The Emperor asked: "Where shall I go to cast off my imperial body? Bodhidharma said: "The Emperor’s own palace is the place to cast it off. The Emperor asked: "Who is it that casts it off? Bodhidharma said: "It is precisely because there is one who casts it off that you do not believe me. The Emperor asked: "What is the primary meaning of the Noble Truths? Bodhidharma said: "Vast and empty, nothing is attained. The Emperor did not understand and consequently sent him away. Bodhidharma crossed the Yangtze River and went to Shaolin Temple on Mount Songshan. After nine years, he faced a wall and sat in meditation without speaking. One day, the Second Patriarch, Huike, approached him and stood in the snow until his feet were cut to the bone. He then bowed and said, "Please, World-Honored One, take pity on my ignorance and grant me the Dharma. Bodhidharma said, "Bring forward your mind, and I will pacify it for you. Huike said, "When I seek my mind, I cannot find it. Bodhidharma said, "I have already pacified your mind for you. Huike thereupon experienced great awakening. Bodhidharma then transmitted the robe and bowl to him and said, "The Tathāgata entrusted me with the supreme Dharma-eye treasury and wondrous mind-ground seal to hand down to you. You must uphold it and propagate it widely; do not let it be extinguished. He further instructed him, saying, "After my passing, when the Dharma declines, there will be a barbarian king who will destroy the True Dharma. At that time, you should go south to the land of the Han, where the Dharma will flourish. He then passed away at the age of seventy-two. His remains were enshrined in a stupa at Shaolin Temple. Later, the Emperor regretted his previous actions and sent envoys to invite him back three times, but he would not return. The Emperor then had a statue of him carved and enshrined in the Jingming Monastery. It is said that whenever the Emperor was troubled by state affairs, he would gaze upon the statue and find peace of mind. This is the primary meaning of the Noble Truths. It is not something to be found through intellectual speculation or verbal expression; it is realized only through the direct pointing of a master and one's own self-awakening. To ask about the primary meaning while leaning toward the secondary is like seeking the moon in the sky while looking at its reflection in the water. To realize that the primary meaning is right here before one, without needing to seek it elsewhere, is to truly see the Buddha-nature. This is the ultimate teaching of the patriarchs. It is not a matter of words or logic, but of directly seeing into one's own nature and attaining liberation. This is the true lineage of the Buddhas and patriarchs. It is not something to be grasped through the intellect or conceptualized through the mind. It is the very lifeblood of all sentient beings. To understand this is to understand the primary meaning of the Noble Truths. To fail to understand this is to remain mired in the secondary. Therefore, the ancients said: "If you wish to know the Buddha, look at your own face before the mirror. This is the primary meaning of the Noble Truths. It is not something that can be described in words or depicted in form. It is the original face of all people. To realize this is to enter the gate of the Buddhas and patriarchs. It is to attain the great freedom and ease of the Way. It is to transcend birth and death and reach the other shore. It is to be free from all delusions and afflictions.
